elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 expressly limits audits to “not more than once per 12 months.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 30 days' advance notice of an audit.
The audit notice must be in writing.
Audits must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 expressly limits audits to “during business hours.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires the audit to be conducted “by an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires an independent auditor “bound by confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that “Vendor bears audit costs” unless the specified exception applies.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs only where underpayment exceeds five percent for the audited period.

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor may not directly access Customer systems.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 expressly provides that “Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly.”

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The limitation to not more than once per 12 months satisfies the once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 15 days' advance notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The required 30 days' written notice exceeds the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 assigns audit costs to Vendor unless its stated underpayment exception applies.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 10%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 permits cost shifting when underpayment exceeds 5%, including underpayments above 5% but not exceeding 10%.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement, including the frequency, written-notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, confidentiality, 5% cost threshold, and no-direct-access protections. It does not satisfy the fallback's 10% cost-shifting threshold. The redline is not minimal because it adds the unrequested and potentially ambiguous requirement “off-site where possible.” Otherwise, it preserves the existing audit-cost and information-access terms and removes the prior contradiction concerning direct system access.
